fields.subnational_unit: Santa Rosa neighborhood, Guaruja (coastal city, Sao Paulo state)
fields.population: households in Santa Rosa (6,573 households) grouped by a social development index into seven study groups
fields.sample_size: 393 household questionnaires (minimum 390 computed with a 12% sampling error; group sizes 9-68); 6,573 households in total; blocks selected randomly
fields.effect_measure: structured household questionnaire on perceived access and quality of water, sewage, drainage and waste services, mapped by block group and compared with SNIS administrative data
fields.effect_estimate: Perception varies strongly across block groups. Water supply is the only service judged adequate; drainage and sanitation most need improvement (in one group 86% judged drainage precarious); perceived waste-management quality diverges from administrative data (SNIS: 82.57% water coverage, 70.05% sewage collection, 100% urban waste collection, 45.3% of households at flood risk citywide). The authors argue municipal sanitation plans must be built with participation and local socio-spatial detail.
fields.model_type: descriptive survey with spatialised perception analysis
fields.study_design: cross-sectional household perception survey in one neighborhood (stratified by a social development index) with spatial analysis
fields.section: Full text (Rev. Gestao Ambiental e Sustentabilidade 11(1):e20281): Method; Results; Final considerations
fields.exact_location: Method p8-10 (SDI groups, sample size equation, Table 2); Results p11-22; Final considerations p25

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a household perception survey (393 questionnaires, 7 social-development groups) in the Santa Rosa neighborhood of Guaruja, Brazil, read in full text 2026-10-04. Perceived adequacy of water supply but not drainage or sanitation, with marked within-neighborhood heterogeneity and divergence from administrative data. One neighborhood, descriptive.
